entities.summary:
Vinitharius, a figure of the Greuthungian Goths around 375-376 AD, is mentioned in Getica by Gothic historian Jordanes.

 According to Jordanes, Vinitharius succeeded Ermanaric (Hermanaric) as the new king of the Greuthungi.

 Ammianus Marcellinus, however, reports that Ermanaric was succeeded by Vithimiris.

 The succession of Vinitharius and Vithimiris reflects the complexities of the Greuthungian Gothic politics and the power struggles within the empire.

 Vinitharius's reign was likely short-lived, as he was eventually succeeded by Vithimiris, marking a significant turning point in the history of the Greuthungi.

 The legacy of Vinitharius and Vithimiris can be seen in the subsequent Gothic history, which was shaped by the power dynamics of the Greuthungian Goths and their interactions with other European tribes.

 The story of Vinitharius and Vithimiris serves as a reminder of the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the ancient world, and the complex forces that shaped the course of human history.
